name: Software / SaaS company
description: A software product or online service: pricing plans, features, customer stories, questions, documentation and terms to download and job openings, with facts about the free trial, data hosting, uptime, integrations, support and security.

questions.question: Can people try the product for free? For how long and on what terms?
questions.help: For example "14 days, no card needed", "free plan up to 3 users" or "none – a demo on request".

questions.question: Where is your customers' data stored – in which country or region, and with which provider?
questions.help: For example "EU – data centres in Frankfurt (AWS)". Business customers often check this before they sign up; write only what is true today.

questions.question: Do you commit to an uptime level in your contracts? Which one, and for which plans?
questions.help: Only what your terms actually promise, e.g. "99.9 % per month on the Business plan". Leave it empty if you give no commitment.

questions.question: Which tools and services does the product connect to?
questions.help: Separated by commas; add "API" or "webhooks" if you offer them. Only integrations that work today.

questions.question: How and when can customers reach your support?
questions.help: For example "e-mail and chat, Mon–Fri 9–17 CET; phone on the Business plan".

questions.question: Do you have a public status page? Give its address.
questions.help: Leave it empty if there is none.

questions.question: Which security or data-protection certifications or audit reports do you currently hold?
questions.help: Only certificates or reports you actually hold and that are valid, e.g. "ISO/IEC 27001 (valid until 2027)". Leave it empty if there are none – never write "compliant" without one.

audit.message: Add your pricing plans with what each includes – visitors compare them before they sign up.
The pricing plans have not changed for a year – check that prices and features still match the product.
Say where customer data is hosted – business customers ask before they sign up.
Say how and when customers reach your support.
Publish your terms of service – customers accept them when they sign up; check what your law requires of them.
Publish a privacy policy – the service processes your customers' data; check what data-protection law requires of it.

claude: Visitors of a software site want to know what the product does and for whom, what it costs, whether they can try it, where their data lives and how to get help – lead with the problem it solves and a clear path to the plans and the trial, and keep trial, hosting, uptime, support and integrations as facts so they read the same everywhere. The services collection holds the features: one item per feature, described as what the user can do. Write concretely, without buzzwords. Never invent customers, logos, testimonials, user counts, uptime figures, integrations, prices or security claims – a certification or "compliant with…" only when the owner confirms it is held and current. Customer stories need the customer's consent. Terms, privacy policy and a data processing agreement belong in the document library; what they must contain depends on law – say it should be checked.
